best_for: People who need to hide what they read from their network, ISP or employer, or reach sites that are blocked where they live.

points.title: Three hops and no history
points.text: Tor Browser sends traffic through three relays, so anyone watching your connection sees only that you use Tor. It isolates each site, and cookies and history are cleared when you close it.

points.title: Gets past blocks
points.text: It can reach sites your government, ISP or home network blocks, and opens .onion sites that only work over Tor. Where Tor itself is blocked, the project explains how to connect through bridges.

points.title: Some habits break the protection
points.text: The Tor Project asks you not to add extra add-ons, not to run a separate VPN alongside it, and not to torrent over Tor. Treat it as a browser for private reading, not your everyday one.

points.title: Free and open source
points.text: It is MPL-2.0 licensed and costs nothing. There is no account and no paid tier.

points.title: Linux is offered, just not here
points.text: The project publishes Linux builds for x86_64 and aarch64 next to Windows and macOS, each with a signature you can check. This site lists Windows and macOS only.

points.title: No admin rights on Windows
points.text: The Windows installers here are per-user, in 32-bit and 64-bit builds. The Mac download is one universal .dmg.

points.title: Older Windows builds kept
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 76 versions. macOS lists only the current release.
